Here’s what’s going on, using the live page (navigation + snapshot worked; screenshot failed in this environment) and the code.

## Why the header sits on top of the image on wider cards

**1. The project card is a 4-row grid with equal row height**

For `variant === "project"` the card uses four equal fractional rows:

```49:53:/home/gonzalo/gonzalopozo.github.io/components/public/grid-item.tsx
            <Card className={cn("size-full min-h-0 min-w-0 overflow-hidden bg-card rounded-4xl", className, {
                "text-card-foreground py-6 bg-card": variant !== "map",
                "gap-0 p-0 py-0": variant === "map",
                "grid grid-cols-1 grid-rows-4 pt-0": variant === "project"
            })}>
```

In Tailwind, `grid-rows-4` is `repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr))`, so **each row gets one quarter of the card’s height** (for a grid whose height is set by the layout, e.g. react-grid-layout).

**2. The hero image scales with width, not with “one quarter of the card”**

The image is a fixed-aspect placeholder (2:1):

```56:57:/home/gonzalo/gonzalopozo.github.io/components/public/grid-item.tsx
                        <Image src={"https://placehold.co/1200x630.png"} alt={"Project image"} width={1260} height={630} />
```

With default `next/image` behavior, the image **grows in height as the card gets wider** (same aspect ratio, full width). The **first row’s height does not grow with width** — it stays **25% of the total card height**, which is fixed by the grid item’s row span and `rowHeight` in `portfolio-grid.tsx`.

**3. Overflow + paint order looks like “overlap”**

On a **narrow** cell, the image’s height can still fit under that 25% bar. On a **wide** cell (e.g. item `e` spans 4 columns vs `c`/`d` at 2 columns), the **same** total height and **same** four rows mean row 1 is still only 25% tall, but the image **needs more vertical space** than that. The `<img>` **overflows** its grid area into the space where row 2 (the header) lives.

The header is the **next** sibling in the DOM, so it **paints on top** of the overflowing image. That reads as “the card header overlaps the image,” even though the real issue is **the image is too tall for row 1** under equal `1fr` rows.

**Summary:** Wider cards make the image taller (aspect ratio × full width), while `grid-rows-4` keeps the image row at a fixed **share** of the card height. The image overflows that row; `CardHeader` sits in the next row and draws above it.

**Direction for a fix (if you want to change it):** Constrain the image to the first row (e.g. wrapper with `min-h-0 overflow-hidden` and `className="h-full w-full object-cover"` on `Image`, or `fill` + `object-cover`), or stop using four equal `1fr` rows (e.g. `auto` for the image row and `1fr` for the rest) so the image row isn’t capped at 25% of the card.
